pairs: JavaScript / Node.js / Express
Language / runtime with host facilities / web framework. Name which layer owns the behavior.
Concurrency / parallelism
Overlapping progress / simultaneous execution. Waiting on I/O and executing CPU work are different cases.
async function / CPU offload
Promise/coroutine semantics do not automatically move computation to another thread or process.
Promise.all / transaction
Collecting asynchronous results does not make external effects atomic or roll them back.
await / cancellation
Waiting for a result is separate from stopping work; cancellation may not undo a committed effect.
TypeScript type / runtime schema
Static checking helps program construction; external values still need validation at runtime.
JSON parsing / authorization
Syntactically valid JSON can contain wrong types, excessive values and attacker-selected roles.
Authentication / authorization
Establish identity / decide whether that identity may perform this action on this resource now.
JWT / encryption
JWT is a token representation family; signing/integrity and JWE encryption are different properties.
Cookie transport / CSRF protection
A browser-attached credential requires an intentional cross-site request policy, not just HttpOnly.
CORS / access control
Browser response-sharing policy does not replace API authentication and resource permission.
OAuth / OpenID Connect
Delegated authorization / an identity layer on OAuth. Explain the actual flow and verified claims.
Idempotency / event deduplication
Repeatable intended business effect / recognizing a repeated event identity. Define scope and durable state.
Unique constraint / required field
Uniqueness and non-null/existence are separate rules; engine/index semantics matter.
Index / faster every query
An index supports particular access patterns and adds write/storage cost; inspect the plan.
SQL NULL / zero
Unknown/absent value is not numeric zero; counts, predicates and aggregates can behave differently.
Single-document atomicity / multi-document transaction
One update boundary does not protect an invariant spanning several independent documents.
Cache / canonical state
An optimization or derived copy is not automatically the durable authority for permissions or balances.
TTL / immediate revocation
Expiration bounds some lifetimes; it does not instantly propagate deletion or permission changes.
Queue / worker
Durable dispatch mechanism / code that performs work. Accepted enqueue is not completed execution.
Acknowledgement / committed effect
Delivery bookkeeping and the business transaction can fail at different points.
Container / virtual machine
Process isolation using a host kernel differs from a guest-kernel machine boundary.
Liveness / readiness
A process can be alive yet unable to accept useful traffic; define each probe deliberately.
TLS / application permission
Encrypted authenticated transport does not decide which document or operation a user may access.
Environment variable / safe browser secret
Configuration location does not guarantee confidentiality; bundling, logs and responses matter.
React render / commit
Computing a UI description differs from applying updates; render should not perform external effects.
SSR / Server Components
Initial HTML rendering and a server-side component execution model solve different concerns.
Next.js cache / tenant isolation
Cache scope and keys must preserve the permission/freshness contract; behavior is version-sensitive.
Embedding model / generative model
Vector representation supports retrieval/comparison; text generation is a different operation.
Similarity / supported answer
A numeric retrieval score is not proof of relevance, freshness, permission or factual support.
Workflow checkpoint / effect dedupe
Restored execution state does not automatically make an external side effect safe to repeat.
Graph / workflow graph
Domain relations and execution transitions have different meanings, invariants and storage needs.
Virtual node / data replica
Another placement token is not another physical server or a durable copy of the key data.
Consistent placement / balanced traffic
Stable ownership and even key counts do not prevent hot keys or uneven request costs.
Throughput / goodput / latency
Completed work, useful successful work and completion time are distinct measurements.
Reported metric / reproduced result
A resume statement and a workload-specific independently executed measurement have different evidence.

rapid_fire.question: Trace a backend request in one sentence.
rapid_fire.answer: Client sends HTTP; the server validates identity/input, authorizes the resource/action, runs application/data work and produces a response. Name dependencies, state ownership and failure boundaries rather than treating the controller as the whole backend.

rapid_fire.question: What makes a closure useful?
rapid_fire.answer: A function retains access to its lexical environment. Use it for controlled state or callbacks, but reason about retained references and stale values. It does not automatically copy every captured object.

rapid_fire.question: Does spread clone nested objects?
rapid_fire.answer: No. Object spread copies top-level properties; nested references remain shared unless handled separately. D05 demonstrates the alias. Choose update semantics rather than assuming every value should be deeply cloned.

rapid_fire.question: Does Promise.all undo successful work after rejection?
rapid_fire.answer: No. It reports aggregate failure without transactional rollback or automatic cancellation. D03 records effects from other started work. Protect business effects at their own durable transaction/idempotency boundary.

rapid_fire.question: Can async filter enforce permissions?
rapid_fire.answer: A synchronous Array.filter does not await an async predicate. The returned Promise is truthy, so D14 keeps every input. Resolve validated decisions first or use a deliberate asynchronous filtering flow with appropriate bounds.

rapid_fire.question: Does a type assertion validate an API payload?
rapid_fire.answer: No. A compile-time assertion does not prove external runtime values match the claimed type. Parse and validate the boundary, then use narrowed types internally. Do not derive tenant or role authority from untrusted JSON.

rapid_fire.question: When should you prefer unknown to any?
rapid_fire.answer: For values whose shape has not been established. unknown requires checking/narrowing before use; any bypasses many checks. Neither replaces domain validation, authorization or limits on input size.

rapid_fire.question: Why can Node serve several waiting requests?
rapid_fire.answer: I/O can make progress through runtime/OS facilities while JavaScript handles other callbacks. JavaScript execution in one event loop is still constrained; long synchronous CPU work can delay unrelated requests.

rapid_fire.question: How do you handle CPU-heavy parsing?
rapid_fire.answer: Measure where CPU/time is spent, reduce unnecessary work, and consider bounded workers/processes or background jobs when needed. async syntax alone does not offload computation. Account for payload size, queue limits and cancellation.

rapid_fire.question: Why does middleware order matter?
rapid_fire.answer: It determines which state/checks exist before a handler and how errors propagate. Parsing, identity, resource permission, rate limits and error handling need deliberate ordering, with framework-version behavior checked.

rapid_fire.question: Why separate controller, service and data access?
rapid_fire.answer: It clarifies HTTP translation, application invariants and persistence responsibilities. These can be modules in one application; separate files do not imply microservices or remote transaction boundaries.

rapid_fire.question: What makes an API retry safe?
rapid_fire.answer: The operation semantics and durable business identity, not only its status code. A failed transport may hide a committed write. Bound attempts/deadline and use appropriate idempotency or reconciliation.

rapid_fire.question: What should pagination define?
rapid_fire.answer: Stable ordering with a tie-breaker, page/cursor contract, limits and behavior as data changes. Scope the query before pagination. A large offset may have cost and consistency trade-offs.

rapid_fire.question: What must token verification check?
rapid_fire.answer: The configured cryptographic verification and relevant issuer/audience, time and purpose claims, plus current session/revocation policy. Decoding alone is not verification. Exact requirements depend on the token/trust design.

rapid_fire.question: Does refresh rotation finish the session design?
rapid_fire.answer: No. Define previous-token invalidation, concurrent refresh behavior, replay detection, family revocation and expiry. A newly issued token does not establish that older credentials became unusable.

rapid_fire.question: Where does tenant isolation apply?
rapid_fire.answer: Across resource queries, file/object access, caches, job payloads, vector/graph reads, citations and derived responses. Derive identity from a verified boundary; apply current action/resource permission, not only a UI filter.

rapid_fire.question: Does CORS protect an API from nonbrowser clients?
rapid_fire.answer: No. It controls browser response sharing under origin rules. Authentication, authorization, CSRF policy and server-side validation remain separate. Do not use a successful preflight as proof of permission.

rapid_fire.question: Why verify a webhook using the raw body?
rapid_fire.answer: The signature covers the exact message bytes under the relevant secret/algorithm. Parsing and reserializing can change those bytes. After verification, validate the business state and apply a durable deduplicated effect.

rapid_fire.question: What happens after a write succeeds but its acknowledgement is lost?
rapid_fire.answer: The outcome is ambiguous to the caller. Retrying without a stable operation identity can repeat the effect. Recover the stored result or reconcile authoritative state rather than assuming the operation failed.

rapid_fire.question: What is the mutable-default trap?
rapid_fire.answer: A default mutable value is created at function definition and can be reused across calls. D07 returns the same list twice. Use a per-call value when isolation is intended.

rapid_fire.question: Does calling Python async def run its body immediately?
rapid_fire.answer: It creates a coroutine; its body runs when awaited or appropriately scheduled. D10 contrasts with the JavaScript async prefix in D01. Neither syntax inherently creates another CPU thread.

rapid_fire.question: Why can an async FastAPI endpoint still block?
rapid_fire.answer: It may call synchronous blocking I/O or CPU work directly on the event loop. Select compatible async dependencies or an appropriate execution boundary. An arbitrary sync helper is not automatically offloaded merely because the framework supports sync routes.

rapid_fire.question: Is a response-lifetime background task a durable queue?
rapid_fire.answer: No. Process/request lifetime work can be lost during failure or restart. Durable jobs require persisted identity/state, retry/acknowledgement semantics and recovery appropriate to the operation.

rapid_fire.question: Does an ORM eliminate query planning?
rapid_fire.answer: No. Inspect generated SQL, query counts, N+1 patterns, indexes and transaction boundaries. Convenient object access can still cause many round trips or lock contention.

rapid_fire.question: Do default serializers enforce every permission?
rapid_fire.answer: No. Validation and serialization are separate from tenant/object/action policy. Review queryset scoping, create/update authority and nested-resource behavior with positive and negative tests.

rapid_fire.question: What does an index plan establish?
rapid_fire.answer: How the engine intends to access data for that query under the observed schema/statistics. A plan alone is not a production latency guarantee; executing/profile tools and representative data require their own evidence.

rapid_fire.question: Is read balance then update balance safe under concurrency?
rapid_fire.answer: Not by itself. Protect the condition and effect with an atomic statement, suitable lock/version/constraint or transaction strategy. Explain isolation, retries and the relevant business invariant.

rapid_fire.question: When is a MongoDB update atomic?
rapid_fire.answer: At the relevant single-document operation boundary. Invariants spanning multiple documents may need a transaction or another design. Define the actual write/update shape and deployment capabilities.

rapid_fire.question: Why can a unique-index assumption fail?
rapid_fire.answer: Null, missing fields, partial/sparse configuration, compound keys and engine semantics change the identity contract. D12 executes SQLite behavior only; review the actual MongoDB index instead of transferring that result.

rapid_fire.question: What does a cache key need?
rapid_fire.answer: Every dimension that changes the permitted/current value, such as tenant, resource, representation or revision, under a documented coherence policy. Adding a TTL does not fix an incomplete key or revoked access.

rapid_fire.question: How do retries affect background work?
rapid_fire.answer: A job can be delivered again or finish after a newer revision exists. Use stable effect identity, bounded work, persisted state and generation-aware publication/reconciliation. Acknowledging delivery and committing business state are separate events.

rapid_fire.question: What survives container replacement?
rapid_fire.answer: Only state stored in an appropriate persistent external store or configured persistent mount, according to its lifecycle. The writable container layer and in-memory variables should not be assumed durable.

rapid_fire.question: Why does localhost fail inside a container?
rapid_fire.answer: It identifies that container/network namespace, not automatically the host database or another container. Use the intended service/network address and verify listener/binding/firewall configuration.

rapid_fire.question: What is graceful draining?
rapid_fire.answer: Stop assigning new work, allow admitted work a bounded grace period, then terminate under a defined policy. Readiness, open connections, long requests and worker/process cleanup all affect the result.

rapid_fire.question: Does TLS make the application secure?
rapid_fire.answer: It protects the specified transport/trust boundary. Resource authorization, credential handling, input limits, CSRF and business correctness remain application responsibilities.

rapid_fire.question: Why distinguish user and service identity?
rapid_fire.answer: A worker or BFF may authenticate as a service while acting for a user/tenant. Verify both the caller capability and the permitted resource operation; do not let a broad service credential bypass tenant policy.

rapid_fire.question: Does a managed queue imply exactly one effect?
rapid_fire.answer: No. Design for its documented delivery/retry behavior and protect the effect separately. Bound concurrency/backlog and include recovery after a commit/ack gap.

rapid_fire.question: What belongs in a meaningful CI gate?
rapid_fire.answer: Checks that catch relevant regressions: contracts, authorization negatives, transaction/replay failures and build/runtime behavior. A passing pipeline only supports what it actually checked in its recorded environment.

rapid_fire.question: How do you report performance?
rapid_fire.answer: State workload, successful goodput, errors, latency distribution, duration, resources and measurement boundary. Compare equivalent before/after runs; an average or peak requests/s value alone is insufficient.

rapid_fire.question: Why can a state value look stale in a handler?
rapid_fire.answer: A render supplies a snapshot used by its callbacks. Understand closure capture and state-update semantics; use the appropriate updater or effect dependency model. Reassigning a variable does not directly render new UI.

rapid_fire.question: How do you prevent an old search response overwriting a new one?
rapid_fire.answer: Track current request identity/generation and reject stale completions, with cancellation where useful. Guarding UI acceptance is still needed when cancellation is delayed or cannot undo backend work.

rapid_fire.question: Are Client Components rendered only in the browser?
rapid_fire.answer: That label identifies a client-capable boundary, not a universal claim that initial HTML never involves the server. Explain the specific Next.js version, route/render flow and hydration; keep secrets out of client bundles.

rapid_fire.question: Can server-side caching ignore identity?
rapid_fire.answer: Only when the value is truly shareable under the defined policy. User/tenant data needs correct scope, current permission and freshness handling. Check version-specific cache behavior instead of relying on a memorized default.

rapid_fire.question: Does structured model output authorize a tool call?
rapid_fire.answer: No. Validate arguments, derive trusted identity, check action/resource permission and apply budgets/idempotency outside the model. A syntactically valid requested action can still be forbidden or unsafe to repeat.

rapid_fire.question: What must an AI budget count?
rapid_fire.answer: The actual workflow: input/output usage, tool/model retries, images or other units, concurrency and maximum steps/deadline. Estimates and settled provider usage are separate, with explicit pricing/version assumptions.

rapid_fire.question: What makes a citation acceptable?
rapid_fire.answer: It must identify source evidence that is current, permitted and actually supports the answer. A formatted source ID or returned chunk alone does not establish those conditions.

rapid_fire.question: Can an old ingestion worker publish after a newer upload?
rapid_fire.answer: Only if the publication policy incorrectly permits it or explicitly supports that historical generation. Guard current source/generation state and canonical read acceptance; reconcile late work and deletions.

rapid_fire.question: Why distinguish exact retrieval from ANN?
rapid_fire.answer: Approximate indexes trade search work against possible missed neighbors. Evaluate with representative scoped queries and a defined exact baseline. Recall under a fixture is not universal model/retrieval quality.

rapid_fire.question: Does matching dimension prove embeddings are compatible?
rapid_fire.answer: No. Model/version, normalization/metric, preprocessing and the intended semantic space also matter. Matching vector length alone does not justify mixing generations or establish answer quality.

rapid_fire.question: What does a checkpoint restore?
rapid_fire.answer: Persisted workflow state under the framework/storage contract. It does not automatically deduplicate effects outside that state. Explain resume/replay identity and recovery around external commits.

rapid_fire.question: When is a framework useful?
rapid_fire.answer: When its composition, state, persistence or retrieval abstractions simplify a problem you can already trace. Compare against plain code and account for configuration, debugging and version coupling.

rapid_fire.question: Why anchor and bound graph queries?
rapid_fire.answer: To limit fan-out/work and make the requested relationship meaning explicit. Validate tenant/path/source scope, handle cycles/duplicates and inspect actual plans for the relevant query shape.

rapid_fire.question: Does MERGE replace identity constraints?
rapid_fire.answer: No. Pattern matching/creation semantics and database constraints have different roles, especially under concurrent writes. Separate stable identity from mutable properties and use the appropriate schema guarantees.

rapid_fire.question: Do virtual nodes replicate data?
rapid_fire.answer: No. They add placement tokens for a physical member. Replication, migration, freshness and write authority require separate mechanisms.

rapid_fire.question: Does balanced key ownership guarantee balanced requests?
rapid_fire.answer: No. A hot key, larger objects or expensive operations can dominate one owner. Measure traffic/cost distribution separately from distinct-key counts and remapping.

rapid_fire.question: How do you defend a resume metric?
rapid_fire.answer: Give its denominator/window, original source, workload/tool and scope, then distinguish reported claims from independently reproduced results. Do not replace original evidence with a similar learning-fixture number.

rapid_fire.question: What if the original implementation detail is unavailable?
rapid_fire.answer: State the supported claim, identify the missing artifact and explain the mechanism/proposed design without inventing history. M28 records unresolved route counts, titles, topology and measurement details.

rapid_fire.question: How do estimates guide design?
rapid_fire.answer: Make workload/unit assumptions explicit, calculate QPS/bandwidth/storage or average in-flight work, then identify the likely bottleneck. Validate assumed per-instance capacity with representative measurements before treating it as a result.

rapid_fire.question: Do local checks establish production capacity?
rapid_fire.answer: No. They establish selected behavior in their fixtures. Production scale, provider semantics, deployment security and real model quality require matching evidence; do not add counts across chapters as a universal reliability score.

rapid_fire.question: How should you justify a technology choice?
rapid_fire.answer: Tie it to an access pattern, invariant, execution constraint or team/operational need. Name a reasonable alternative and the trade-off. Avoid using a brand name as a substitute for the mechanism.

debugging.title: CPU work behind async
debugging.symptom: All Node routes slow during PDF parsing, even though the parser function is async.
debugging.answer: Measure event-loop delay/CPU and isolate the synchronous segment. Reduce/bound payload work and use a suitable bounded worker/job boundary. Verify unrelated-request latency and cleanup; adding await to CPU work is not a fix.

debugging.title: Tenant-blind cache
debugging.symptom: A document response is correct after cache expiry but belongs to another tenant on a warm hit.
debugging.answer: Inspect cache identity and acceptance policy before tuning TTL. Include required scope/revision dimensions, recheck current permission as designed, invalidate incorrect entries and verify cross-tenant/revoked-access negatives.

debugging.title: Duplicate payment credit
debugging.symptom: A captured-payment webhook delivered twice adds balance twice.
debugging.answer: Verify raw-body authentication and business/order identity, then make dedupe plus credit effect durable and atomic. Test duplicate, concurrent and out-of-order delivery and the commit/ack failure window.

debugging.title: Ambiguous timeout
debugging.symptom: The client sees 504; the order row exists; a retry creates another order.
debugging.answer: Use a stable scoped operation identity and stored outcome/reconciliation. Inspect where the deadline expired and which effect committed. Test lost acknowledgements; a timeout response does not prove rollback.

debugging.title: Pool waiting
debugging.symptom: Individual SQL queries are quick, but API latency rises sharply with concurrency.
debugging.answer: Separate pool acquisition, query execution, locks and serialization in traces. Check leaked/long-held connections, N+1 and dependency capacity. Validate bounded admission and representative end-to-end latency before adding pools/replicas.

debugging.title: Vanishing sheet children
debugging.symptom: A score patch updates one field but removes children that were not present in the incoming row.
debugging.answer: Recover the snapshot/patch contract and compare nested before/after payloads. Apply explicit merge/array/deletion semantics with validation and rollback policy. Prevent recurrence and reconcile historical loss separately.

debugging.title: Blocking async route
debugging.symptom: A FastAPI async route calls a blocking SDK and unrelated requests wait.
debugging.answer: Profile the dependency call and its execution context. Use an appropriate async API or bounded offload/request execution strategy. A normal helper called directly inside async code remains a direct call.

debugging.title: Stale browser search
debugging.symptom: Search B finishes before search A; the UI eventually displays A.
debugging.answer: Tag requests/generations and accept only the current result, with cleanup/abort where appropriate. Test controlled out-of-order responses and unmount. Aborting transport is not a guarantee of backend rollback.

debugging.title: Shared server cache
debugging.symptom: A Next.js server response changes after login but the cached result is reused across accounts.
debugging.answer: Establish the version/render/data-cache boundary, then check key/scope and current permission. Use the intended private/no-cache or correctly scoped policy and negative tests; server execution alone does not ensure isolation.

debugging.title: Late ingestion worker
debugging.symptom: Document revision 2 is ready; a slower revision-1 worker later replaces its retrieval evidence.
debugging.answer: Carry stable source/generation identity, guard publication against current canonical revision and reject stale evidence at acceptance. Test late completion, retry and tombstones across every derived store/cache.

debugging.title: Graph permission shortcut
debugging.symptom: Vector retrieval is scoped, but graph expansion reveals an unauthorized intermediate entity.
debugging.answer: Scope the entire path and relevant source evidence, not just start/end nodes. Define relationship permissions and fan-out bounds. Verify cross-tenant intermediates, shared/revoked sources and citation acceptance.

debugging.title: Checkpoint repeats a charge
debugging.symptom: A workflow resumes from a saved state and sends the same external charge again.
debugging.answer: Locate the external commit versus checkpoint gap. Use durable business-effect identity and replay-safe adapter state; reconciliation may be needed after lost acknowledgements. A checkpoint is not a global transaction.

debugging.title: Container localhost
debugging.symptom: The app connects to the database on the host, but fails with localhost inside its container.
debugging.answer: Trace network namespaces, server bindings, service addresses and firewall rules. Confirm configuration at runtime without leaking secrets. Verify intended connectivity/readiness rather than simply exposing more ports.

debugging.title: Failed graceful shutdown
debugging.symptom: A rolling restart interrupts admitted requests despite a readiness endpoint.
debugging.answer: Trace when readiness/drain changes, when new work stops and when termination occurs. Define a bounded grace period and cleanup for active resources. Test an existing held request and new arrival during drain.

debugging.title: Balanced keys, overloaded node
debugging.symptom: The hash ring has even ownership counts but one backend serves almost all requests.
debugging.answer: Measure key popularity and request cost. Identify a hot key; more virtual tokens cannot split its single-owner traffic. Choose a domain-appropriate cache/replica/coalescing/capacity strategy with freshness semantics.

debugging.title: Misleading throughput win
debugging.symptom: A new version reports more requests/s while p99 and errors rise.
debugging.answer: Compare successful goodput and latency/error objectives under equivalent offered workload and resources. Check arrival model, retries, generator limits, duration and cold/warm phases. A larger throughput headline alone does not establish an improvement.

self_test.question: Trace one authenticated note read through client, BFF/API and data store.
self_test.answer: Identify credential verification, trusted tenant, resource permission, query/cache scope and response. Name a failure boundary.

self_test.question: Explain JavaScript async prefix versus Python coroutine creation.
self_test.answer: Use D01/D10: JavaScript runs the synchronous prefix when called; Python creates a coroutine until awaited/scheduled. Neither offloads CPU automatically.

self_test.question: Validate a payload with a string limit and client-supplied admin role.
self_test.answer: Parsing/type assertions are insufficient. Validate types/bounds and derive authority from verified identity/policy.

self_test.question: Show a concrete closure or nested-alias bug.
self_test.answer: Explain lexical/reference behavior using D05 or an earlier chapter example and choose a deliberate update/freshness policy.

self_test.question: Decide whether a failed POST may be retried.
self_test.answer: Trace possible commit, stable business identity, saved outcome, deadline/attempt policy and reconciliation.

self_test.question: Design expiring and revocable candidate access.
self_test.answer: Scope purpose/resource/tenant, verify signature or opaque token, check authoritative expiry/revocation and handle redemption/rate-limit races.

self_test.question: Stop another tenant from reading a cached document.
self_test.answer: Scope cache/query and current permission; test warm/cold, shared/revoked and wrong-tenant cases.

self_test.question: Handle duplicate/out-of-order payment events.
self_test.answer: Authenticate raw payload, validate business state, and atomically dedupe/apply the intended effect. Do not trust the browser success page.

self_test.question: Protect a balance from two simultaneous spends.
self_test.answer: Make condition and effect atomic under an appropriate database strategy, with operation identity and documented failure recovery.

self_test.question: Interpret COUNT(*), COUNT(value) and nullable UNIQUE.
self_test.answer: Predict D11/D12 and state the executed SQLite scope. Check actual target-engine/null/index semantics before applying the result.

self_test.question: Explain a slow API with fast individual queries.
self_test.answer: Separate pool waits, locks, query count, network and application work; inspect plans and representative traces.

self_test.question: Choose whole-batch rollback or row quarantine for ingestion.
self_test.answer: State the business invariant, source identity, error reporting, checkpoint/replay policy and historical reconciliation.

self_test.question: Preserve a file and configuration across container replacement.
self_test.answer: Name persistent storage/configuration/secret boundaries, container networking and resource/readiness checks.

self_test.question: Explain draining during a deployment.
self_test.answer: Stop new work, permit admitted work within grace, then terminate/clean resources. Verify failure behavior for long operations.

self_test.question: Propose a meaningful CI regression gate.
self_test.answer: Use a concrete contract/security/replay/transaction failure case and state the environment/version and what remains untested.

self_test.question: Fix a stale React request completion.
self_test.answer: Accept only the current request/generation, clean effects and use cancellation where appropriate; explain render snapshots.

self_test.question: Separate Next.js rendering, runtime and data-cache policy.
self_test.answer: Describe the project version and server/client/Edge/Node boundaries. Scope sensitive data and keep secrets out of bundles/responses.

self_test.question: Authorize and budget a model-requested tool.
self_test.answer: Validate arguments, derive identity, enforce resource/action policy, bound steps/concurrency/cost and guard side effects against replay.

self_test.question: Publish current RAG evidence after duplicate/late jobs.
self_test.answer: Use canonical source/revision/tombstone state, stable jobs and guarded publication/read acceptance across stores.

self_test.question: Evaluate vector retrieval without assuming score means truth.
self_test.answer: Define permission-scoped candidate/ground-truth sets, exact/ANN baseline, recall/relevance and answer/source support.

self_test.question: Resume a workflow without repeating a business effect.
self_test.answer: Explain checkpoint versus external transaction state, durable effect identity and reconciliation of an ambiguous outcome.

self_test.question: Bound a tenant-scoped graph traversal.
self_test.answer: Anchor permitted entities, validate intermediate nodes/edges/source scope, limit depth/fan-out and handle cycles/duplicates.

self_test.question: Defend consistent-hash movement and proxy throughput.
self_test.answer: Define configuration/corpus/denominators and traffic costs, then report goodput/latency/errors/resources and original-versus-fixture evidence.

self_test.question: Give a two-minute project explanation with one unresolved detail.
self_test.answer: State personal ownership, request/state flow, choice, failure/test and result boundary. Label missing source evidence explicitly.

two_hour_route: Select weak modules and trace one request

scope: Editorial prompts/checkpoints and planning arithmetic, not executed production scenarios or user assessment.
